original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: If an in-memory copy of research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py raises only the dimension guard from 27 to 36, does batch size 20 on the P112 36-generator basis return the eight-word set whose positive-word SHA256 is ff8861dab18040c03d403a860773218df7c120d03770d701afb61b78c941e3d3?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a measured speedup that keeps coverage. Priority revision 8 says faster output is equivalent coverage only after the sets are compared. Open PR #7034 records that the published engine refuses this basis before the lane loop, and leaves the dimension-36 copy unrun. This package runs that copy at batch size 20. It records no speedup and leaves the selected conditional exponent unchanged.
bottleneck_link: A faster iterator can certify a code only when it returns that code's low-weight words. On this 36-generator basis the published engine never reaches the intersection arithmetic. The copied guard lets that arithmetic be compared with the recorded eight-word set. The selected conditional exponent is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop after one batch-size-20 stream of the dimension-36 copy on this basis. Do not edit research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py, raise the 65536-batch guard, search a shorter generating set, time a speedup, or rerun the E6, D6, or E7 censuses.
evidence: The rebuilt kernel has generator-list SHA256 c93a6ec3f6d61b3bbf4086218c723761e517bc42ac2c26f551436d271a081e9d. The seven partition supports have SHA256 ff8861dab18040c03d403a860773218df7c120d03770d701afb61b78c941e3d3. The copy differs from engine.py by the four characters of the two guard numerals, 27 to 36, in the one statement need(index < 27, "dimension exceeds 27"). The published file still raises dimension exceeds 27 on this basis. At batch size 20 the copy admits all 36 generators, uses 20 lane generators and 65536 high-offset batches, and its exhausted stream is zero followed by those seven supports in the recorded increasing order. Every yielded word has weight 0 or 16 and lies in the frame code. Batches 1 through 19 still raise batch count exceeds 65536. No codeword census beyond this stream was run. Registered stream times on this host were 127.082 s and 116.527 s; those times are not a speedup claim.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: If a second opt-in copy also raises the unchanged 65536-batch guard, does one other batch size on this same 36-generator basis return the eight-word set with hash ff8861dab18040c03d403a860773218df7c120d03770d701afb61b78c941e3d3?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Batch size 20 is the only legal size at which 36 generators pass both the new dimension guard and the old batch-count guard. A different lane split is a different stream.
open_questions.first_step: In a separate harness, admit one other batch size, for example 16, without editing research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py, and compare that one stream with this hash.
open_questions.blocked_by: The published batch-count guard rejects every batch size below 20 on this 36-generator input. This package does not raise that guard.

open_questions.question: Does the yield order of this batch-size-20 stream equal the yield order of research/e7-bitsliced-exhaustion/binary.py low_weight_words on the same basis and weight bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package compares sets. Equal sets can still be emitted in different orders, and the bitsliced iterator was not called.
open_questions.first_step: Run the two iterators once each at batch size 20 and compare the sequences, not only the sets.
open_questions.blocked_by: The bitsliced batch is a second 2^36 lane enumeration. Open PR #7007 already records that iterator's set, and this package does not rerun it.
